belief: I have to be perfect or I'll lose my job.
origins: Perfectionism at work often starts in childhood, where mistakes were punished or achievement was praised. A real workplace layoff, a harsh review, or a close call can cement it. We work late, double-check everything, and feel nervous after every small error.
teaches: The psalmist says, “He knows our frame; He is mindful that we are dust.” Solomon notes, “There is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.” Proverbs says, “Though a righteous man may fall seven times, he still gets up.” God told Paul, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” God does not expect perfection from us at work, and most employers do not either. Excellence is worthwhile; perfection is impossible and exhausting.
self_statements: One mistake and I am out.
I must work twice as hard.
errors: Believing that anything short of perfect is failure.
Imagining that one error will cost my job.
Insisting that I should never make mistakes.
questions: What is the actual standard in my workplace, and how do I know?
Have I seen coworkers make mistakes and keep their jobs?
What happened the last time I made an error?
What does perfectionism cost me in time, health, and relationships?
What would “good and reliable” look like?
What does God expect of me?
truth: I do not have to be perfect to keep my job or to be valued. God knows I am dust, and my worth does not depend on flawless work. I can aim for good, honest work and learn from mistakes without fear.
hw_truths: I can get up after mistakes.
log: Each day, name one task you finished at “good enough” and what happened.
actions: Ask your manager what “good” looks like.
Do one task without a third check.
Record what actually happens after minor errors.
Leave on time at least twice this week.
prayer: Father, I fear making mistakes. You know I am dust. Free me from perfectionism, and help me work honestly and rest in Your grace. Amen.
hw_questions: What happened after my last mistake?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God knows I am dust, so I do not have to be perfect.”
